title: OpenSharing becomes the default cross-org AI-asset sharing protocol by Q3 2027
body: On June 10, Databricks and the Linux Foundation announced OpenSharing, a vendor-neutral open protocol extending Delta Sharing to cover agent skills, AI models, and unstructured data, enabling zero-copy cross-organizational sharing of AI assets without proprietary marketplaces. The founding partner roster is commercially significant: OpenAI, SAP, Stripe, Atlassian, and Amadeus. This is not a niche data-engineering standard — it places OpenSharing squarely at the intersection of enterprise SaaS (SAP, Atlassian), payments infrastructure (Stripe), and frontier model providers (OpenAI). The business thesis is that these founding partners anchor a network-effect dynamic: each enterprise that adopts OpenSharing to share agent skills with a partner avoids building a bespoke point-to-point integration, which in turn reduces the switching cost of choosing OpenSharing-compatible vendors. Historically, vendor-neutral protocols backed by a major cloud data incumbent (Databricks) plus a neutral foundation (Linux Foundation) and a critical mass of SaaS leaders move from launch to de-facto standard in 12-24 months when the use case has obvious bilateral demand — file formats (Parquet), table formats (Delta, Iceberg), and container runtimes (OCI) followed this arc. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by Q3 2027 at least three additional Fortune 500 SaaS or cloud vendors publicly announce OpenSharing compatibility or integrations — documented in a Databricks or Linux Foundation press release, a GitHub merge to the official OpenSharing spec, or a named announcement at a data or AI conference. What does NOT count: individual customer implementations without vendor-level commitment; integrations built on Delta Sharing alone without the OpenSharing AI-asset extension; non-Fortune-500 adopters; or 'coming soon' roadmap items without a generally available implementation. The counter-risk is that hyperscalers (AWS, Microsoft, Google) each back competing proprietary asset-sharing surfaces, fragmenting the market and preventing OpenSharing from crossing the critical SaaS-partnership threshold.

reasoning.landing: by Q3 2027: three or more additional Fortune 500 vendors announce OpenSharing compatibility
reasoning.plain_language: Big companies joined a new open standard for sharing AI tools, so it will likely become the go-to way companies share AI with each other.

summary: Databricks and the Linux Foundation launched OpenSharing on June 10 with founding partners including OpenAI, SAP, Stripe, and Atlassian — a vendor-neutral protocol for sharing agent skills, AI models, and data across organizations. The combination of a major data platform, a neutral foundation, and enterprise SaaS leaders mirrors the adoption arc of Parquet and Delta. By Q3 2027 at least three additional Fortune 500 vendors should publicly commit to OpenSharing compatibility.
